column3: NASB follows the critical text without “Lord” before the second “Christ Jesus”; it adds “of” and “who is.”
NASB follows the critical text without “our” after “Father.” A full-width colon appears in the NASB text.
NASB restructures the verse; “warn” is rendered “instruct,” and “other doctrines” is “strange doctrines.”
NASB follows the critical text (“speculations”); it adds “mere” and “furthering” and renders “stewardship” as “administration.”
NASB adds “our.”
NASB renders “having missed the mark” as “straying” and “meaningless discourse” as “fruitless discussion.”
NASB adds “even though” and renders “confidently assert” as “make confident assertions.”
Close to the Greek.
NASB renders “insubordinate” as “rebellious” and “murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers” as “those who kill their fathers or mothers.”
NASB renders “enslavers” as “kidnappers.”
NASB renders “the gospel of the glory” as “the glorious gospel.”
NASB follows the critical text without “and”; it renders “Thankfulness I have” as “I thank” and “esteemed” as “considered.”
NASB follows the critical text; “insolent” is rendered “a violent aggressor,” and it adds “even though.”
NASB renders “surpassingly increased” as “was more than abundant.”
NASB renders “saying” as “statement” and “of full acceptance worthy” as “deserving full acceptance.”
NASB reads “Jesus Christ,” the order of other manuscripts; the critical text has “Christ Jesus.” “Pattern” is rendered “example.”
NASB follows the critical text without “wise”; “King of the ages” is rendered “King eternal.”
NASB renders “charge” as “command,” “child” as “son,” and “war the good warfare” as “fight the good fight.”
NASB renders “having cast away” as “have rejected.”
NASB renders “be disciplined” as “be taught.”
